hallowed-ground.summary: A Gettysburg licensed guide website project: historical vs after-dark pathways, five tours, an OpenLayers battlefield map, and a Sage + WooCommerce handoff.
hallowed-ground.challenge: A Gettysburg licensed guide website has to sell small-group walking, bus, hike, lantern, and private sunrise tours without looking like a food-tour sibling brand. Call-to-reserve sites lose the people who plan at night on their phones.
hallowed-ground.approach: Working HTML as the front-end contract for a later Sage + WooCommerce theme. Home splits daylight vs lantern walks; the catalog filters five tours; The Area is an OpenLayers battlefield map.
hallowed-ground.result: A clickable demo with a distinct identity. When WordPress ships, WooCommerce picks up the same pages.

first-shot.summary: A walking-tour project with a calendar booking flow, add-ons, and demo payment.
first-shot.challenge: A tour with limited daily slots needs to show what's actually available — a static contact form oversells sold-out dates and frustrates guests before they even arrive.
first-shot.approach: A calendar-driven booking flow: pick an available date, see real time slots, add tickets and upgrades with a live total, and check out.
first-shot.result: A project that turns a scheduling headache into a self-serve calendar, upsells add-ons at checkout, and confirms instantly.

field-of-valor.summary: A Gettysburg tour project grown into a full bespoke website. Small groups, licensed guides, the story in order — fast, accessible, easy to run.
field-of-valor.challenge: A good tour deserves a site that feels as considered as the tour itself. The project needed a real multi-page home, a clear way to show seven different tours, and the trust a first-time visitor looks for — without a page builder.
field-of-valor.approach: An archival-heritage look built as a bespoke WordPress theme. Tours are a reusable content type with their own fields, so adding or editing one takes minutes.
field-of-valor.result: A fast, WCAG 2.2 AA site with seven tour pages, a booking flow, and a marketing landing page — the kind of site a real Adams County operator could own and run.

keystone-homes.summary: A Sage WordPress theme for farms, land, and historic homes: grid and map listings, acreage filters, and financing tools a broker can actually run.
keystone-homes.challenge: Land and farm buyers need different filters — acreage, township, lot type — and a map. A generic home-search template can't show a 40-acre parcel the way it deserves.
keystone-homes.approach: A grid-and-map listings tool built for rural property, with acreage and township filters as query args, a land-loan estimate, financing pre-qualification, and a call scheduler. Vanilla JS widgets, no page builder.
keystone-homes.result: A WordPress starting point that speaks land buyers' language, shows parcels on a map, and moves serious buyers from browsing to a booked call.
keystone-homes.audience: Land offices, farm brokerages, and agents selling acreage or historic homes who cannot use a suburban MLS skin.
keystone-homes.architecture: Listings render as a grid and a map, with acreage, township, and lot-type filters as query args. The land-loan estimate and pre-qualification widgets are vanilla JS. Intended production stack is Sage 11, a listing CPT or imported feed, and Rank Math for titles and schema.
keystone-homes.handoff: You own the theme and the listing fields. Brokers edit parcels, photos, and copy in wp-admin. I document the listing schema so the next developer can extend filters without touching the template.

ridgeline-realty.summary: A realty project with filterable listings, a live mortgage calculator, and support tools.
ridgeline-realty.challenge: Buyers browse listings on their phones and bounce when a site is slow, unfilterable, or missing the numbers. Those leads go straight to Zillow — and the agency never sees them.
ridgeline-realty.approach: A fast, filterable listings experience with a search bar, a live mortgage calculator, and easy schedule-a-showing and contact-an-agent tools.
ridgeline-realty.result: A project that holds buyers with real search and real numbers, then converts them with one-tap showing requests and direct agent contact.

ridgeline-outfitters.summary: An outdoor gear shop project with filters, quick-view, wishlist, and a cart with a free-shipping bar.
ridgeline-outfitters.challenge: Outdoor shoppers compare gear across ten browser tabs. A store with no filters, sizes, or wishlist loses them to Amazon before they ever notice the local expertise.
ridgeline-outfitters.approach: A gear-forward shop with category filters, quick-view, size selection, a wishlist, and a cart with a free-shipping progress bar.
ridgeline-outfitters.result: A project that competes with big retailers on convenience while winning on local knowledge and battlefield-trail credibility.

diamond-ridge.summary: A downtown mercantile project with a full product shop, slide-in cart, and checkout.
diamond-ridge.challenge: A downtown shop with foot traffic but no online store misses every visitor who wanted 'that candle' shipped home. Generic marketplace listings hid the local, handmade story entirely.
diamond-ridge.approach: A full e-commerce storefront with a slide-in cart and clean checkout, wrapped in a brand that leads with 'locally made' — so the shop keeps selling to visitors long after they've left town.
diamond-ridge.result: A project that opens a second register online, keeps the maker story front and center, and lets a one-time visitor become a repeat customer from anywhere.

diamonds-threads.summary: A vintage-inspired boutique website project with distinctive branding, mobile-friendly shopping, and a clear customer journey for an independent Gettysburg-area retailer.
diamonds-threads.challenge: Most local shop sites bury what you carry, forget to say when you're open, and cram everything onto one slow scroll. A boutique lives on foot traffic, and a phone-first shopper downtown will pick the next door if yours makes them work for the basics.
diamonds-threads.approach: A complete, hand-authored WordPress site — no page builder — around the way people actually shop a local store. Browsable collections, a story worth the trip, and a Visit page with hours, parking, and a map.
diamonds-threads.result: A fast, warm, six-page site a real boutique could open with: collections to browse, a clear reason to visit in person, and local-SEO groundwork for 'boutique in Gettysburg.'

cannon-crumb.summary: An all-day cafe project with a tabbed, filterable menu and a real online-ordering cart.
cannon-crumb.challenge: A busy cafe leaves money on the counter without online ordering — and a wall-of-text menu makes it worse. Regulars wanted to order ahead; first-timers wanted to filter for vegan and gluten-free.
cannon-crumb.approach: An interactive, tabbed and filterable menu with a working online-ordering cart — pickup or delivery, running total, and a clean checkout — so the morning rush moves to the app, not the line.
cannon-crumb.result: A project that captures ahead-orders, answers dietary questions instantly, and turns a static menu into a working storefront that pays for itself.

field-musket.summary: A seasonal tavern project with an editorial, always-current menu and a clear reservation path.
field-musket.challenge: Diners decide on their phones, and a menu trapped in a PDF or a photo is the fastest way to lose them. This tavern's seasonal menu changed faster than its old site could keep up.
field-musket.approach: An editorial, easy-to-read menu the owner can update in minutes, plus a one-tap reservation path and the farm-to-table story that justifies the price.
field-musket.result: A project where the menu is always current, reservations are a tap away, and the local-sourcing story does the selling — no PDF, no stale specials.

pintfield.summary: A Gettysburg creamery website design project with a live 32-flavor Scoop Board, online ordering, three-location details, and owner-scheduled updates.
pintfield.challenge: A multi-location creamery changes flavors every morning, but static menus and unanswered phone calls leave customers guessing what is in the case, which shops are open, and whether cakes or dairy-free options are available.
pintfield.approach: Build around a live Scoop Board: 32 daily flavors, dairy-free and no-sugar-added choices, owner scheduling, online ordering for cakes and cookies, and consistent location details for all three shops.
pintfield.result: A working project that turns everyday customer questions into fast self-service, gives the owner one place to publish flavor changes, and makes ordering or choosing a shop simple on any screen.

reveille.summary: A full farm-to-table restaurant website — menu, reservations, private events and online ordering — built to turn a phone search into a booked table.
reveille.challenge: Most local restaurant sites bury the menu and a way to book under slideshows and out-of-date hours. One long scroll is hard for Google to rank and harder for a hungry visitor on a phone.
reveille.approach: A full multi-page site with a warm farm-to-table design: seasonal menu, reservations, private events, gallery, and online ordering each one tap away. Hand-built WordPress theme — no page builder.
reveille.result: A restaurant site that looks like the room feels and works like a good host — turning dinner searches into booked tables and takeout orders.

cupola-field.summary: A modern boutique hotel project with a live reservation engine and concierge + guest-request tools.
cupola-field.challenge: A hotel site has to answer two questions instantly: is my date open, and can someone help me right now? Most local hotel sites answer neither.
cupola-field.approach: A live reservation engine that recalculates nightly rate and total as guests change dates and rooms, paired with a concierge chat widget and a guest-request checklist.
cupola-field.result: A project that turns browsing into booking with instant pricing, and turns questions into answers with an always-on concierge.

lantern-laurel.summary: A nine-room heritage inn project with a direct booking bar and a warm forest-and-brass identity.
lantern-laurel.challenge: Small Gettysburg inns bleed booking commission to the big travel sites — and those sites bury the property's own story. Guests couldn't even check dates without a phone call during business hours.
lantern-laurel.approach: A warm, heritage-forward design that puts a direct booking bar front and center, so guests reserve on the inn's own site. Rooms, rates, and the neighborhood are one scroll away.
lantern-laurel.result: A project that could recover commission on every direct booking, reads beautifully on a phone, and lets a first-time guest feel the welcome before they arrive.

willoughby.summary: A full boutique-inn website — eight rooms with rates, a real booking flow, the inn's story, a Gettysburg area guide and a gallery — built to win direct bookings.
willoughby.challenge: Small inns lose booking commission to the big travel sites — and most inn websites make it worse by burying rooms and rates behind slideshows on one long scroll.
willoughby.approach: A full multi-page site with a moody, dramatic design: eight rooms with rates, a booking flow, the inn's story, a Gettysburg area guide and a gallery. Hand-built WordPress theme — no page builder.
willoughby.result: An inn site that feels like the place and makes booking direct the obvious choice — keeping the full nightly rate with the owner.

herr-ridge.summary: A warm, three-room bed-and-breakfast project — built and live as a full multi-page site you can click through.
herr-ridge.challenge: A small B&B competes on charm and personality — which most template sites flatten into something generic.
herr-ridge.approach: A soft terracotta-and-sage cottage design, hand-built as a bespoke WordPress theme. Three rooms, each with its own page, plus breakfast and things-to-do sections and an easy book-a-room path.
herr-ridge.result: A site as inviting as the cottage itself — fast, accessible (WCAG 2.2 AA), and built to turn a weekend search into a booked stay.
